description: This line plot illustrates the accuracy (ACC %) of five different methods—Base, MEND, FT, IKE, and ROME—as a function of the co-occurrence number, which is plotted on a logarithmic scale ranging from 10⁰ (1) to 10³ (1000). The y-axis represents accuracy in percentage, ranging from 60% to 80%. The Base method (black line with circle markers) starts at approximately 64% accuracy and increases steadily to about 71%. The MEND method (brown line with diamond markers) begins at around 70% and rises to approximately 80%. The FT method (blue line with triangle markers) starts at about 65% and increases to roughly 73%. The IKE method (red line with triangle markers) begins at approximately 67% and rises to about 75%. The ROME method (green line with square markers) starts at around 74% and increases to approximately 82%. All five methods show an upward trend as the co-occurrence number increases, with ROME consistently achieving the highest accuracy and Base the lowest across the entire range.
